blocks.text: Brackenridge Civil Group Inc is a civil engineering firm working out of the county seat, and it has done the same plain work since it was founded in 1996. We design the grading, drainage, roadway, and utility improvements a site needs before it can be built. Our clients are the public bodies and private builders who put up work in this part of the county: municipal public works departments, a regional water authority, and private developers. This overview sets out what the firm does, how it does it, and shows the work through one representative project. It is written to claim only what is true and no more.

The firm's work divides into a few plain lines, though on most jobs they run together. We grade a site so that it sits and drains the way it must, and we prepare the erosion and sediment control that holds the soil while it is disturbed. We design the stormwater management for a site, the pipes and inlets and detention that carry runoff away and meet the county's drainage standards, and we prepare the drainage studies that stand behind them. We lay out roadways, whether a new street in a subdivision or the widening and resurfacing of an existing one, and we design the water, sanitary sewer, and storm utilities that run beneath them. A single subdivision may draw on all of these; a drainage complaint at one intersection may need only a study and a modest fix. We take the small job as seriously as the large one.

A project begins with a walk of the site and a scope set down in writing, so that the client and the firm agree on the work before it starts. The design is done at our own boards and checked before it is issued. Nothing leaves this office until the set has been reviewed and the cover sheet sealed, and that order holds on every job without exception. The construction documents we produce, the drawings and the specifications, are prepared to be built from and to carry a contractor and the county's reviewers through the work without guesswork. Where a set must go before a public body for permit or approval, we prepare it to that body's standards and see it through the review.

The firm is small, and its records are kept close. The drawings are held in the firm's project folders alongside the paperwork that belongs to each job. Executed agreements come back to the office, often by fax, and Mark Barrett logs each one, scans it on the flatbed, and files it with the plans it belongs to, so that a project folder holds the whole of a job and not merely its sheets. The standard details and border sheets that every set is built from are kept current and shared, so the firm's drawings look and read the same from one project to the next.

One recent engagement gives a fair picture of the work. For {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}}, we carried the site grading and stormwater design from the first walk of the ground through the county's review, coordinating the set so that the grading and the drainage agreed before either was issued. We offer it as one example of how the firm works and not as an account of our full book of business. We do not, as a matter of practice, discuss one client's project with another.

If you have a site that needs civil design, the next step is a conversation and a look at the ground. Direct inquiries to Mark Todd, Principal Engineer, who will arrange to walk the site and set a scope in writing before any work begins.
